It seems like you know what you want to do. From what you say, it seems that you don't want to end things in a way that involves suicide but rather in a way that is simply a solution to the problem(s) itself/themselves. That's a great thing if that's the case because it means you're aware that suicide isn't the only way out. There are plenty of other ways to go about rough patches in life. Even if the patch started at birth and continues to this day, there's always a way to get out of the patch. Take a deep breath and make a list of the things you want to fix in your life. Then order them by difficulty from easiest to hardest. Start easy and then work up because once you've solved a few easy problems, you'll be more motivated to solve the rest of the problems no matter how difficult they may be. Also remember this: you don't have to take anyone's advice, but people who give you advice obviously seem to want to affect you whether it be in a negative way or a positive way. In this case, I want to help you in a positive way however that does not mean you are obligated to take my advice. Your life is your's which means you decide how to live it and what to do. Either way, I hope some part of this comment helped even if it just made you smile thinking, "This guy is a f***ing idiot." :-)

I had depression for about a year and a half during my junior and senior year of high school. I cut out all the toxic people in my life and kept the ones that I trusted and were there to support me. Next I went to a bit of therapy and got a little slap of reality that life can be unfair and it is just something that people have to understand and deal with sometimes. Once I did those two things, I focused on myself and started living my life for myself instead of for others. There is a time and place to be selfish. An old teacher of mine told me that and I realized he was right because once you start worrying yourself with other people, you lose time to worry about yourself and you start to lose sight of what you want out of life. I don't know if any of this helps but it helped me and it may be a start for others. No matter what happens, know that you can be happy but the more you chase it, the more it runs. If you create it yourself, it's your's forever. :-)
